tool_summary: Ubuntu's sandboxed package/app installer. Snaps are more isolated than deb packages by design (confinement via AppArmor/seccomp), but --classic disables that confinement, and installing from a non-default channel can pull less-reviewed builds.
platform_notes: snap is Ubuntu-specific (though the snapd daemon is available on some other distributions).

rules.description: The --classic flag disables snap's default confinement (AppArmor/seccomp sandboxing), giving the installed application the same level of system access as a traditionally packaged application. This removes the primary security benefit snap packaging otherwise provides.

The --dangerous flag allows installing a local .snap file without signature verification, typically used for locally-built or unpublished snaps. This bypasses the Snap Store's review and signing process entirely.

Installs a snap package. Confined by default (AppArmor/seccomp), which somewhat limits blast radius compared to traditional package installation, but still fetches and runs code with the invoking system's snapd privileges.
Manages snap packages. Read-only subcommands (list, find, info) do not alter system state.
